items.label: Art. 5 – Principles relating to processing
items.interpretation: Any agent that processes personal data must respect purpose limitation, data minimisation and storage limitation by design. This is the baseline for retention rules and only-the-data-you-need filters.

items.label: Art. 6 – Lawfulness of processing
items.interpretation: Requires a lawful basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests) for each processing operation; the admin should record the basis for each data source.

items.label: Art. 9 – Special categories of personal data
items.interpretation: Prohibits processing sensitive data (health, ethnicity, religion, political opinions, trade-union membership, biometric, sexual orientation) except under narrow conditions. Hard-block ingestion of these categories into agents unless explicitly permitted.

items.label: Art. 13 – Information at data collection
items.interpretation: Defines mandatory information for data subjects; used to generate notice text when agents collect data directly.

items.label: Art. 17 – Right to erasure
items.interpretation: Supports deletion workflows for logs and profiles generated by agents.

items.label: Art. 20 – Data portability
items.interpretation: Supports export features for profiles produced by agents.

items.label: Art. 22 – Automated decision-making and profiling
items.interpretation: Triggers human-in-the-loop pathways where agent outputs might produce legal or similarly significant effects.

items.label: Art. 25 – Data protection by design and by default
items.interpretation: Basis for hard-coded compliance layer; influences default settings for all agents.

items.label: Art. 32 – Security of processing
items.interpretation: Supports security controls around agent logs and data access.

items.label: Art. 35 – Data protection impact assessment
items.interpretation: If an agent exhibits high-risk patterns (systematic profiling, monitoring, sensitive data), flag DPIA required.

items.label: Art. 5 – Prohibited AI practices
items.interpretation: Hard bans on manipulative systems, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, untargeted facial scraping, crime-risk prediction based only on profiling, emotion recognition at work or school, sensitive biometric categorisation, and certain real-time biometric identification.

items.label: Art. 6 – High-risk classification
items.interpretation: Used with Annex III to classify agents as minimal, limited, high or unacceptable risk.

items.label: Art. 9 – Risk management system
items.interpretation: Requires systematic risk management for high-risk agents: identify, analyse, evaluate, mitigate.

items.label: Art. 10 – Data and data governance
items.interpretation: Influences training and evaluation data for ML-dependent agents (representative, free of errors).

items.label: Art. 12 – Record-keeping
items.interpretation: Requires logging of events; drives immutable agent logs.

items.label: Art. 13 – Transparency and information to deployers
items.interpretation: Supports instructions-for-use and limitations attached to each agent.

items.label: Art. 14 – Human oversight
items.interpretation: Requires meaningful human oversight; used to enforce escalation patterns.

items.label: Art. 26 – Obligations of deployers
items.interpretation: Guides deployers own duties; relevant to console messaging.

items.label: Art. 27 – Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment
items.interpretation: For certain public-body high-risk deployments; console should flag FRIA required.

items.label: Art. 50 – Transparency (AI identity)
items.interpretation: Requires user awareness when interacting with AI or deepfakes; supports AI disclosure messages.

items.label: Art. 1 – Object and purpose
items.interpretation: Ensures AI lifecycle activities are consistent with human rights, democracy and rule of law.

items.label: Art. 9 – Accountability and responsibility
items.interpretation: Supports accountability mappings and logging.

items.label: Art. 10 – Equality and non-discrimination
items.interpretation: Requires measures against discriminatory outcomes; underpins bias routines for agents.

items.label: Art. 11 – Human oversight and safeguards
items.interpretation: Reinforces EU AI Act Art.14; justifies human override and escalation patterns.

items.label: Art. 16 – Risk and impact management
items.interpretation: Supports ongoing risk and impact assessments for agents.

items.label: Art. 7 – Respect for private and family life
items.interpretation: Constrains worker and customer monitoring and intrusive agents.

items.label: Art. 8 – Protection of personal data
items.interpretation: Constitutional basis for data protection rules applied to agents.

items.label: Art. 21 – Non-discrimination
items.interpretation: Supports prohibitions on discriminatory scoring or ranking by agents.

items.label: Art. 8 – Right to respect for private and family life
items.interpretation: Key for workplace surveillance and monitoring limitations.

items.label: Art. 10 – Freedom of expression
items.interpretation: Relevant when agents classify or moderate content.

items.label: Proportionality & Do No Harm
items.interpretation: Supports bounded agents, proportional data use and harm reduction.

items.label: Fairness & Non-Discrimination
items.interpretation: Underpins bias mitigation requirements.

items.label: Human Oversight & Determination
items.interpretation: Pairs with GDPR and EU AI Act oversight obligations.

items.label: Transparency & Explainability
items.interpretation: Supports explainability statements for agents.

items.label: Pillar II – Corporate responsibility to respect
items.interpretation: Justifies Human Rights Due Diligence for agent deployments.

items.label: Pillar III – Access to remedy
items.interpretation: Supports grievance mechanisms linked to agent decisions.

items.label: C87 – Freedom of association
items.interpretation: Constraints on agents tracking or penalising union activity.

items.label: C98 – Collective bargaining
items.interpretation: Protects workers from retaliation; shapes HR agent behaviour.

items.label: C111 – Discrimination (Employment and Occupation)
items.interpretation: Supports bias controls in recruitment, promotion and evaluation agents.

llmHelper.promptTemplate: You are a Treaty-Following compliance assistant for the @Human platform. You are given an agent description, system prompt and guardrails. Using the Treaty Compliance Layer, select all relevant treaties and articles that must govern this agent. Always include all hardwired articles. Then add optional ones that are relevant given the agents function (HR, finance, customer support, security, marketing, field service, public authority, etc.), the personal data categories used, and the kinds of decisions the agent supports. Return JSON with selectedTreaties (array of treaty IDs) and selectedArticles (array of article IDs).
